To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Chinese adult learners of L2 English exhibit lexicalized structural priming of reduced RCs.
Chinese adult learners of different education levels primed reduced relative clauses in English, and that this effect was lexically specific.
L2 comprehension of reduced relative clauses is primed, and that the priming effect is specific to verbs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what kind of knowledge and processing mechanisms adult learners of a language bring to bear on the task of learning a second language.
the question of whether L2 comprehension primig is similar or different from L1 comprehension primig.
the question of whether L2 comprehension of reduced relative clauses is lexically specific.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study are consistent with lexicalist models, and that the results are not consistent with the Clahsen and Felsers' (2006a, b) model.
L2 sentence comprehension is similar to L1 comprehension in some aspects and differs in others, depending on the specific linguistic structure under consideration.
the same mechanisms are involved in the processing of L1s and L2s, but that the extent of their use depends on the learner's education level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lexicalist account is supported by the current study and that the L1 and L1 comprehension primed are the same.
lexicalist models of L1 sentence processing are compatible with L2 sentence comprehension, and that L2 comprehension primed by lexicalized structures may be similar to that of native speakers.
L2 processing of reduced relative clauses is similar to L1 processing, and that L2 learners can use the same mechanisms as L1 speakers to understand these structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
L2 learners can be primed by syntactic information, but only if it is lexically specific.
the mechanisms underlying L2 comprehension primiging are very similar to those underlying L1 comprehension primiging, at least for reduced relative clauses.
the mechanisms involved in L1 sentence comprehension are not necessarily different from those in L2 comprehension.
